independent_deductions: From exponential definitions, sinh derivative is (exp(x)+exp(-x))/2=cosh; cosh derivative is (exp(x)-exp(-x))/2=sinh. Difference of squares expands to exp(x)exp(-x)=1. No circular-cosine minus sign transfers to cosh.

cosh(x)>=1 follows from (exp(x/2)-exp(-x/2))^2>=0. For every real v, t=v+sqrt(v^2+1)>0 and x=ln(t) yield sinh(x)=v and cosh(x)=sqrt(v^2+1); this parametrization covers exactly the right branch. A left branch is not supplied by cosh(x).

Sum/constant/product/quotient/chain formulas are correct under their differentiability and domain conditions. Differentiating u*v^(-1) gives u-prime/v-u*v-prime/v^2. A constant c is required for the constant-multiple rule.

Implicit cubic gives 3y^2*y-prime+3y^2+6xy*y-prime=0. The curve forbids y=0, so y-prime=-y/(y+2x) wherever a differentiable y(x) branch and nonzero denominator are available. Denominator zero forces x=cuberoot(2), y=-2*cuberoot(2). Parametrization x(y)=8/(3y^2)-y/3 is valid for every curve point since y!=0; dx/dy=-16/(3y^3)-1/3 vanishes exactly there, and dy/dy=1. Its tangent direction is therefore vertical. Local invertibility away from that point must be justified or explicitly conditioned in teaching; conditional differentiation alone cannot prove existence.

Principal arcsin has range [-pi/2,pi/2]. On interior inputs its cosine is positive, so inverse derivative =1/sqrt(1-x^2). Endpoints have no finite slope. Principal arctan ranges (-pi/2,pi/2); sec^2=1+x^2 gives derivative 1/(1+x^2) on all real inputs. Inverse notation is not reciprocal.

Sine and cosine derivative proofs use radian-angle addition formulas and the two displayed limits. For sine the quotient becomes sin(x)*(cos(h)-1)/h+cos(x)*sin(h)/h; cosine becomes cos(x)*(cos(h)-1)/h-sin(x)*sin(h)/h. Limits give cos(x), -sin(x). Sec derivative is sin(x)/cos(x)^2=tan(x)sec(x) where cos(x)!=0.

For x>0 and fixed real r, x^r=exp(r ln x) is differentiable and yields r*x^(r-1). Log differentiation gives the same expression but needs positivity and differentiability; the exponential route supplies those. It does not establish a universal formula on negative x or at zero.

Final exp(x arctan x) derivative is exp(x arctan x)*(arctan x+x/(1+x^2)) on all real x. This follows by outer chain and inner product rules, retaining both product terms. Source rhetoric about differentiating anything is not universal differentiability.
